title: Microsoft's diagnostic agent beats physicians in a simulation, not in a clinic
friendlyTitle: Microsoft's diagnostic agent beat doctors in a simulation, not in a clinic
summary: Microsoft says MAI-DxO, a panel of AI agents that question, order tests, and debate a diagnosis, is more than twice as accurate as physicians using textbooks and the internet on complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine. On emergency-department presentations from MIMIC-IV-ED, it reports 1.7 times the accuracy of physicians. The results are published in Science. A prospective study with Beth Israel Deaconess, where patients would use the system directly, is still ahead. Microsoft is also working with Mayo Clinic on a healthcare foundation model.
friendlySummary: Microsoft says MAI-DxO, a group of AI agents that ask questions, order tests, and debate a diagnosis, was more than twice as accurate as doctors using textbooks and the internet. That comparison used hard cases from the New England Journal of Medicine. On emergency-department cases from a research dataset, Microsoft reports 1.7 times the accuracy of doctors. The results are in the journal Science. A hospital study with Beth Israel Deaconess, where patients would use the system themselves, has not happened yet. Microsoft is also working with Mayo Clinic on a healthcare model.
whyItMatters: This is not a diagnosis you should act on. It is a simulation on hard published cases, and Microsoft's own next step is a hospital study that has not reported results. If the numbers hold with real patients, the practical change would be fewer tests to reach the same answer. Until then, it is a research result with a strong headline and no clinic behind it.
